blocks.text: Indo SMC Ltd makes and sells three things. (1) Sheet Moulding Compound (SMC) enclosures: meter boxes, distribution boxes, junction boxes, SMC sheets and chequered plates [F] (AR2026 p.48). (2) Fibre-reinforced plastic (FRP) gratings, pultruded profiles and cable trays [F] (AR2026 p.48). (3) An 'electrical components' range of current and potential transformers (HTCT, HTPT, LTCT), metering cubicles, LT/HT distribution boxes, feeder pillars and busduct [F] (PPT Jun 2026). It earns money by selling manufactured products against purchase orders and tenders. FY26 revenue was all 'sale of products'; the Rs 2.10 cr of consultancy and installation income booked in FY25 did not recur [F] (AR2026 p.83).

**FY26 is now an electrical-components business with an enclosure business attached.** The 'CT PT Products' segment produced Rs 222.02 cr of Rs 309.74 cr revenue (71.7%), SMC Rs 63.97 cr (20.7%) and FRP Rs 23.75 cr (7.7%) [F] (AR2026 p.89) [E]. Management describes the end market as power distribution utilities (DISCOMs, state electricity boards), EPC contractors and industrial customers [MC] (AR2026 p.49). It says about 60% of the business is government-based [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). Exports on an FOB basis were Rs 3.29 cr in FY26, about 1.1% of revenue [F] (AR2026 p.92) [E]. Revenue by state and customer concentration are not disclosed. On the Q4 call, management named Maharashtra, Gujarat and Karnataka as its main current states [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). The Q4 FY26 call was held on 22 May 2026 and is cited throughout as CALL Jun 2026.

Listing status: the company was incorporated in 2021 [F] (AR2026 p.5). It listed on the BSE SME platform on 21 January 2026 after a Rs 91.95 cr fresh issue at Rs 149 per share [F] (AR2026 p.29). As an SME-listed company it reports half-yearly, so the 'quarterly' columns in our statements data are actually the half-years H2 FY25 and H2 FY26 [F] (NUMBERS) (PPT Jun 2026). The SEBI corporate-governance report requirements do not apply to it [F] (AR2026 p.37). The prospectus was not available to us. The evidence base is therefore one audited annual report, two call transcripts, one presentation and five years of screener statements, three of which carry meaningful revenue [F] (NUMBERS).

subsections.title: Bear thesis: the strongest reasons not to own it

items: 1. **Growth has consumed cash.** CFO was -Rs 35 cr in FY26 against PAT of Rs 32 cr, and cumulative three-year CFO/PAT is -1.0x with three-year FCF of -Rs 78 cr [F] (NUMBERS). Every rupee of reported profit since FY23 has been reinvested in working capital, and more besides [AI].

2. **Inventory swelled at year-end.** Inventories rose from Rs 17.23 cr to Rs 85.08 cr. Finished goods rose from Rs 4.37 cr to Rs 33.85 cr (7.8x) and raw materials from Rs 6.42 cr to Rs 42.25 cr [F] (AR2026 p.82). Management explains this as a deliberate three-month raw-material stockpile against geopolitical risk [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). That does not explain the finished-goods build [AI].

3. **Statements filed with the bank did not match the books in all eight quarters of FY25-FY26.** In Q3 FY26, book debts reported to HDFC Bank were Rs 4,938.72 lakh against Rs 2,639.35 lakh per books, a gap of Rs 2,299.37 lakh. The stated reason was 'statements without entries of receipts' [F] (AR2026 p.61). The FY25 Q2 gap was Rs 3,068.29 lakh [F] (AR2026 p.94).

4. **The price is above even the bull-case DCF.** At Rs 482 the shares sit 14.9% above the bull value of Rs 410.1 and 44.9% above the base value of Rs 265.5. The reverse DCF implies 37.8% annual sales growth for five years, against a base-case equivalent of 19.8% [F] (NUMBERS).

5. **Published numbers conflict inside the annual report.** The MD's letter cites revenue of Rs 330.82 cr, EBITDA of Rs 49.06 cr and PAT of Rs 31.95 cr, against audited Rs 309.74 cr, Rs 47.65 cr and Rs 32.38 cr [F] (AR2026 p.15, p.68). The MD&A gives ROE as 21.01%; the audited note gives 33.93% [F] (AR2026 p.51, p.86). The Schedule V statement records export performance as 'Nil' while the notes show Rs 328.98 lakh of exports [F] (AR2026 p.25, p.92).

6. **The margin narrative is contradicted by segment data.** Management says CT/PT carries better margins than SMC [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Yet FY26 segment results imply about 12.2% for CT PT against 25.2% for SMC and 12.7% for FRP [F] (AR2026 p.89-90) [E]. Group EBITDA margin fell from 16.9% to 15.4% [F] (AR2026 p.51).

7. **The operating history is very short.** Sales were Rs 1 cr in FY22, Rs 7 cr in FY23 and Rs 28 cr in FY24 [F] (NUMBERS). Two years of scale and one audited post-listing year cannot establish through-cycle economics [AI].

8. **Governance is promoter-dominated, with early-life warning signs.** The MD is also CFO. Four of six directors are promoters or promoter-group shareholders [F] (AR2026 p.30, p.76). An independent director resigned on 6 April 2026, less than three months after listing, and no reason is disclosed [F] (AR2026 p.30). The annual report contains no related-party schedule despite directors' loans of Rs 325.40 lakh [F] (AR2026 p.79).

9. **Demand is government-timed and orders are short-cycle.** About 60% of business is government-based [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). Management is deliberately taking 2-3 month orders because of raw-material volatility [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). The year-end order book covers less than one year of revenue [E].

10. **The shares are illiquid and institutional holders are leaving.** Shareholders numbered 1,334 in June 2026. DII holding fell from 6.79% to 2.65% and FII holding from 0.82% to 0.13% between March and June 2026 [F] (NUMBERS).

blocks.text: [AI] The market appears to treat Indo SMC as a high-return electrical-equipment compounder: the stock is up from a Rs 134 low to Rs 482 and trades on 34.4x trailing earnings [F] (NUMBERS). Our reading of the filings is less flattering. Since FY23 the business has turned every rupee of profit into receivables, inventory and supplier advances. Its fastest-growing segment earns roughly half the margin of the legacy SMC line. Its first annual report as a listed company contains at least a dozen internal inconsistencies, including a Rs 23 cr bank-statement gap. None of this proves anything is wrong with revenue. It does mean the reported growth has not yet been validated by cash, and the price already exceeds our bull-case DCF. The variant view cuts both ways. If H1 FY27 delivers Rs 200 cr+ of revenue with positive operating cash flow and lower inventory, much of the bear case dissolves quickly, because the asset-light fixed-capital model then shows through.

blocks.text: [MC] Management says all products are made by the company itself, not through a subsidiary (CALL Feb 2026). Note, however, that labour charges rose from Rs 2.17 cr to Rs 10.45 cr in FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.85). The MD also referred to 'a lot of job work' being done [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Some production therefore appears to be contracted to outside parties whose identity is not disclosed [AI]. The promoters' earlier composites careers came up on the Feb call. Management says its team came largely from Sintex (transcribed as 'Syntax') and that the family has been in the trade for 30 years [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). No promoter-group operating company is disclosed in the annual report [F] (AR2026 p.28).

[AI] The current business is very young. Revenue was Rs 1 cr in FY22 and Rs 28 cr in FY24 [F] (NUMBERS). CT/PT manufacturing at Nashik only began in 2024 [MC] (PPT Jun 2026). The Ghiloth plant and the expanded FRP lines date from 2025 [F] (AR2026 p.50). So the segment that delivered 71.7% of FY26 revenue has existed for about two years. The capital history is also compressed: two bonus issues and a preferential round in four months of 2024, then an IPO 13 months later [F] (AR2026 p.76). The preferential allotment at Rs 352 equates to about Rs 117 per share after the subsequent 2:1 bonus [E], against an IPO price of Rs 149 and a current price of Rs 482 [F] (NUMBERS). The object-clause expansion in August 2025, the month before the prospectus, added tarpaulins and geomembranes and technical consultancy [F] (AR2026 p.34-35). That suggests the business scope was still being defined at the point of listing [AI].

subsections.title: Production and service chain, step by step

items: 1. Qualification: obtain utility vendor registration and type-test approvals, then bid in DISCOM tenders or quote to private and EPC customers [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). Example: MSEDCL vendor approval for 11 kV metering cubicles [F] (AR2026 p.50).
2. Order intake: tenders allot from January onward; management now prefers Rs 3-50 cr orders with 2-3 month delivery and a price-escalation clause above 5% movement [MC] (CALL Jun 2026).

3. Procurement: resin and glass fibre (SMC/FRP), copper and steel (CT/PT, busduct), and CRGO cores imported from Korea, China, Japan and Taiwan [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Recorded imports were only 1.45% of material consumption [F] (AR2026 p.91).

4. Conversion: SMC compounding and compression moulding at Pirana (Ahmedabad) and Ghiloth (Rajasthan); FRP grating and pultrusion at Pirana; CT/PT winding and assembly, metering cubicles and switchgear components at Nashik [F] (AR2026 p.10, p.49).
5. Testing: in-house laboratories; the lab at Nashik was being expanded with IPO funds [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Testing expense was Rs 41.08 lakh in FY26 [F] (AR2026 p.85).

6. Dispatch and collection: government customers pay on fixed cycles with about 10% advance; private customers pay 20-50% advance on some orders [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). Debtor days were 42 in FY26 [F] (NUMBERS).

blocks.text: [E] FY26 gross margin (revenue less materials consumed and inventory change) was about 26.0%, against 26.3% in FY25 and 38.7% in FY24 (AR2026 p.68; PPT Jun 2026). Value capture is therefore mainly a conversion margin on bought-in copper, steel, resin and cores. The segment data say the conversion margin is highest in SMC: the segment result was 25.2% of segment revenue in FY26, against 12.2% for CT PT [E] (AR2026 p.89-90). [AI] Our reading is that SMC enclosures earn more because moulding tools and utility-specific designs are a modest barrier, whereas CT/PT and busduct are largely copper pass-through. Management's own description of the Lloyd busduct order as 'very low margin' (an analyst's paraphrase that the MD affirmed) is consistent with that reading [MC] (CALL Jun 2026).

[F] Net fixed assets were Rs 21 cr and CWIP Rs 8 cr against Rs 310 cr of sales; fixed-asset turnover was 14.76x (NUMBERS). [F] Buildings carry a gross block of only Rs 1.02 cr, and factory rent was Rs 2.21 cr (AR2026 p.81, p.85). [AI] Most plants therefore appear to be leased. The model is light in fixed assets but heavy in working capital: inventories and receivables totalled Rs 120.83 cr at March 2026, 5.7x net PPE [E] (AR2026 p.67). Rising labour charges and the MD's references to job work point to growing reliance on outside conversion capacity [AI].

blocks.text: [AI] Commodity-like: SMC sheets, FRP gratings and cable trays, busduct and tarpaulin. These are made to standard sizes or specifications, compete mainly on price and delivery, and pass through volatile inputs. Management itself says gratings are 'standard size' and junction boxes are standard [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). Moderately differentiated: utility-approved meter boxes, CT/PT and metering cubicles, where vendor registration and type tests restrict who can bid [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). Differentiation is approval-based, not technology-based. Management confirmed there are no patented or proprietary designs [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). PCVCB, RMU and the larger SMC parts from the 2,000-ton press do not yet exist as revenue lines [F] (AR2026 p.50).

blocks.text: Source: [F] (AR2026 p.89-90). [AI] Two things stand out. First, the CT PT result margin of 12.2% sits below management's 'above 18%' aspiration and well below SMC [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Second, the SMC segment carries Rs 130.78 cr of assets, 58% of the balance sheet, on Rs 63.97 cr of revenue. items: SMC: [MC] H1 was slowed by an extended monsoon and Q4 by resin shortages after March geopolitical disruption; March is normally the peak month (CALL Feb 2026; CALL Jun 2026). [AI] A plausible further factor is that FY25 included one-off compound sales of about Rs 15 cr that management chose not to repeat (CALL Feb 2026).

FRP: [MC] Pultrusion only started after Diwali 2025, and machines were still being added in February-March 2026 (CALL Feb 2026). [AI] FY26 FRP revenue of Rs 23.75 cr implies about Rs 2 cr a month. That is far below the Rs 7-8 cr monthly run-rate targeted in February [E].

[AI] This large, low-margin busduct order explains both the jump in segment revenue and the 12.2% result margin. Strip it out and the remaining CT/PT margin may be higher, but the split is not disclosed.

blocks.text: [AI] All three segments are order-driven. CT PT and metering cubicles are the most tender-dependent: utility allotments come from December onward and execution runs from April [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). SMC meter boxes are also tender-led, though management says it is building a 'retail counter' channel [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). FRP is the most organic, selling to industrial buyers on repeat orders [MC] (CALL Feb 2026). Busduct revenue so far has been project-specific: a Rs 20.89 cr entry order [F] (AR2026 p.50).

blocks.text: Conflicting disclosures: the Schedule V statement attached to the AGM notice gives 'Export Performance: Nil' (AR2026 p.25). The Directors' Report and Note 35 record FOB exports of Rs 328.98 lakh (AR2026 p.36, p.92). The two are not reconciled. An analyst also cited 60-70% of DRHP-period sales coming from Gujarat [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). The DRHP was not available to us and the figure is unverified.

[MC] Management has trial exports of FRP products (cable trays, gratings, pultrusions) to Oman. It plans a Dubai electrical fair from September 2026, has sent samples to the US and Germany, and targets the Gulf, Africa, Europe and the UK (CALL Feb 2026; CALL Jun 2026). It cited a 'USD 79 billion' FRP export market [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). That figure is the global FRP composites market size [F] (AR2026 p.47) and is industry context only. [AI] At 1.1% of revenue, exports are a strategic aspiration, not yet a mix driver. US sales would require UL 94 certification, which management acknowledged is still pending sample approval [MC] (CALL Jun 2026).

[F] Foreign-exchange outgo was Rs 379.84 lakh against FOB earnings of Rs 328.98 lakh in FY26, a small net short position (AR2026 p.36, p.92). [F] The exchange-difference loss was Rs 17.67 lakh (AR2026 p.85). [MC] CRGO cores come from Korea, China, Japan and Taiwan (CALL Jun 2026). Our documents disclose no tariff, anti-dumping or trade-policy action affecting the company. [MC] The main supply shock cited is the Middle East conflict from March 2026, which disrupted resin and petroleum-derived inputs (CALL Jun 2026; AR2026 p.46). Hedging policy: management said copper is the volatile input and is handled through back-to-back pricing, not financial hedges [MC] (CALL Feb 2026).

[F] There are four plants in three states: SMC and FRP at Pirana, Ahmedabad; electrical components at Nashik; SMC at Ghiloth, Rajasthan (AR2026 p.10, p.49). [AI] The CT PT segment, 71.7% of revenue, appears to depend on the single Nashik site. Management said Nashik 'requires some capex and more space' and that a second Nashik plant has started [MC] (CALL Jun 2026). Its address, ownership and capacity are not disclosed.

**Customer concentration is not disclosed** in the annual report, presentation or calls. The MD&A lists 'customer concentration' as a business risk without quantifying it [F] (AR2026 p.53). This is a finding in itself. [AI] A single analyst-cited busduct order of about Rs 100 cr (CALL Jun 2026), set against Rs 309.74 cr of revenue, implies one customer could have been close to a third of FY26 sales. We cannot verify this. The audited busduct order value is Rs 20.89 cr (AR2026 p.50), and the two figures are not reconciled.

blocks.text: [F] At Rs 482 the shares trade above the bear (Rs 119.9), base (Rs 265.5) and bull (Rs 410.1) per-share values from our DCF model, and above every cell of the sensitivity grid (maximum Rs 365.1) (NUMBERS). Scarcity of listed distribution-equipment small caps and a thin, retail-heavy float also play a part [F] (NUMBERS). It is not supported by cash generation, margin trend or disclosure quality.

[AI] For a long-horizon investor, the evidence needed to underwrite the business (positive CFO, stable margins, clean controls, disclosed concentration) is one to two reporting periods away. The current price assumes that evidence arrives favourably. We would re-review at: (1) the H1 FY27 results (half-year to Sep 2026; date not yet announced) for revenue vs Rs 200 cr, CFO, inventory and margin; (2) any equity raise announcement after September 2026; (3) the FY27 annual results and annual report (about May-September 2027) for segment margins, the CARO bank-statement section, the GST key audit matter and related-party disclosure; and (4) major order or approval announcements on the exchange.

summary.one_line: Indo SMC has scaled from Rs 28 cr to Rs 310 cr of revenue in two years on utility CT/PT and meter-enclosure demand, but the growth has not converted to cash, its first listed annual report carries material control and disclosure inconsistencies, and at Rs 482 the shares sit above even the bull-case DCF value of Rs 410.1.
